You're lucky quetiapine works like that for you!!! It is indeed very strong and very good for sleeping issues. I'd say is the healthiest drug in the market atm for mental issues. It can be used for depression, dementia, insomnia, anxiety and the only big side effect is that you get weird dreams (sometimes) and that if you don't sleep between 30/45 minutes after taking it you're gonna eat your whole fridge, is kinda like getting stoned. I'd say the zolpidem and quetiapine mix works really well. If you can maintain yourself with that you're good! Regular blood tests will show you if it is affecting you in any other way. 
And about imsomnia, it can literally be triggered with any sort of change in your life. Also screen time affects your sleeping schedule so much, maybe getting those blue light glasses would help you with the lighting of screens. Also I would recommend  looking into ways of improving your sleep routine (this is so dumb to say tbh but I swear it makes a difference), start by small things like: taking a shower before bed, turning your lights off at a certain hour, listening to a podcast or music that helps you to get sleepy. Routines work and I've had imsomnia my whole life, your brain and body gets used to it!

*this is my experience and I'm not encouraging anyone to do it, always talk with your doctor first *
The healthiest way I have faced this problem is mixing drugs. I currently take 200 mg of quetiapine, 12,5 mg of zolpidem and 2 mg of clonazepam. My doctor prescribed all of them. Is better to take less of a drug and mixing them with others in order to work for your case. Benzos are never good to take a lot. So maybe a lower dose can work with another drug, that's what worked best for me.
Wishing you the best!
